Both reject "", "-", and any non-digit characters, and both accept "0", "1234", and "0042" with the same value.

what_a: Returns true when a monster with the "needs a good weapon" bit (R13/R15) is hit by a weapon whose floor is below half the monster's level found, meaning the weapon is too weak to affect it.
what_b: Runs one party member's combat turn in Mordor, skipping paralysed or dead members, handling Defend and Fight orders, and resolving each weapon's swings against the front living monster, including the weapon-gate check that forces a Defend order when a monster needs a good weapon.
diff: A is a pure predicate that returns true whenever the target has bit 4 and weaponFloor < levelFound/2. B applies that same test only after checkWeaponGate has already failed, and only then does it switch the actor to Defend, clear party.itemOrders[mu], and emit the "combat.gate" message. So B can't stand in for A (A returns true for any such target, while B does nothing unless the gate failed), and A can't stand in for B (A has no side effects and doesn't break the swing loop). Assuming monsterHasBit(m, bit 4) is equivalent to testing m.specialPropertyFlags & (1u << 4), the predicates agree in the branch where both run.

what_a: Decides whether a guild of a given level, teaching a school at a given rate, can reach a spell of a given level, by requiring the guild to be joined and the rate to be positive and checking that spell level times rate does not exceed half the guild level plus 0.5.
what_b: Computes the spell-point cost of casting a given spell for the caster by checking each guild the caster belongs to that can reach the spell, pricing it with the guild's spell rate and the caster's guild spell level, and keeping the cheapest accepted price (raised to the smallest rated level seen), or 0 if no guild can cast it.
diff: A returns a bool (whether a guild reaches a spell level at a given rate); B returns an i32 price (the cheapest accepted cost across the caster's guilds, or 0). Their return types, inputs, and purposes differ, so no call site could swap one for the other.

what_a: Computes the gold fee for uncursing an item as 80% of its base price divided by 0.5, rounded half-to-even and converted into the game's internal currency units.
what_b: Computes the gold fee the General Store charges to realign an item, which is 72% of the item's list price (doubled when realigning more than one step), rounded half-even and converted to currency.
diff: They differ for every positive price. For price 100, A returns 160 gold (1,600,000 Currency), while B returns 72 gold for |alignmentSteps| <= 1 (including 0) and 144 gold for |alignmentSteps| >= 2. B also returns 0 when the item id has no definition, and A has no such case. B takes the absolute value of alignmentSteps, which A has no input for.

what_a: Converts a double into a fixed-point Currency value by scaling by the currency unit and rounding half to even, returning 0 if the result would overflow the range.
what_b: Rounds a double to four decimal places using half-even rounding and returns it as a 64-bit fixed-point integer, with no game meaning of its own.
diff: Inputs where `d * 10000` is at or beyond ±9.2e18, including values in (9.2e18, ~9.22e18] that still fit in i64, and infinities and NaN. For these, A returns 0 while B passes the value to `roundHalfEven`, which gives an out-of-range or undefined result (for example, `d = 1e15`). This assumes `kCurrencyUnit` is 10000 and both use the same `roundHalfEven`, neither of which is shown.

what_a: Returns the index of the first group in the encounter that is still standing (per SRD R5), or -1 if no group is left standing.
what_b: Scales a gold amount by the party's total group count, multiplying by standing/2.0 (so Gold × standing ÷ 2) and returning the result as a currency value.
diff: Not applicable. Function A returns an index (`i32`) of the first standing group, or -1. Function B returns a `Currency` value: the gold divided by the currency unit, multiplied by `standing / 2.0`, then converted back to currency. They take different inputs and return different types, so no input yields matching results.

what_a: Parses a text string into a 1-based party member number and returns false if the text isn't a number or falls outside the valid party size range.
what_b: Parses a string of digits into an integer party slot number between 1 and kPartyMaxSize, returning -1 if the text is not a valid slot.
diff: Both accept exactly the slot numbers 1..kPartyMaxSize written as plain decimal digits (e.g. "1", "12"), but they differ on other inputs. B rejects any string longer than 2 characters, so "001" returns -1, while A accepts it if companionsParseNumber accepts leading zeros. A's handling of "+1", " 1", "-0", and "" depends on companionsParseNumber, which isn't shown, so I can't confirm those agree with B. Also, B signals failure with -1 and A with false plus an out-parameter, so call sites need a form change.

what_a: If the actor's aimed monster group has no standing monsters left, retargets the actor to the first group that still has standing monsters (rule R15).
what_b: Implements R3 of the melee rules: further swings stay on the aimed group while it still has standing members, and otherwise aim shifts to the first standing group.
diff: When the aimed group is not standing and no group is standing, A leaves `actor.order.aimedGroup` unchanged, while B returns `firstStandingGroup(enc)`, which may be -1 or another sentinel (its body is unknown). A also writes the result into the actor, while B returns it, which changes call-site form but not the rule. Whether B matches A elsewhere depends on the unseen `aimMustMove` and `firstStandingGroup` bodies, which I assumed correspond to `!groupStanding` and `standingGroupIndex(ctx, game, -1)`.

what_a: Casts an unsigned size value to a signed ptrdiff_t so it can be used as an iterator offset, with no game meaning.
what_b: Casts a signed 32-bit index to an unsigned 32-bit integer with no game meaning.
diff: A maps size_t to ptrdiff_t and B maps i32 to u32, so they differ in input type, output type, and width. For example, A(5) returns 5 and B(5) returns 5u, but B(-1) returns 4294967295u while A(SIZE_MAX) returns -1.

what_a: Returns true if any equipped worn item that counts for the wearer carries a resistance flag for the given damage kind, which is how the game decides whether that kind of damage is resisted.
what_b: Tests whether an item's resistance bitmask grants resistance to a given damage kind, returning false for out-of-range kinds.
diff: A takes a context, character, and inventory, loops over worn items, and returns true if any equipped, counting item with a definition resists the kind. B takes a raw resistance bitmask and a kind and returns a single bit test. They have different signatures and return different things (an inventory-wide check versus one item's flag test), so no inputs make them interchangeable; A only uses B's logic for each item in its loop.

what_a: Returns a guild's experience-point coefficient from the guild table, which the game's experience rules use when awarding EP to characters of that guild.
what_b: Computes the threshold experience points needed for a character at level x, scaled by the guild's experience factor and the race's experience multiplier, rounded to a whole number (returns 0 for x ≤ 0).
diff: Function A returns only the guild EP coefficient looked up from the guild table, while Function B returns a rounded threshold XP that depends on x, guild, and race. They disagree for every input, for example Human Nomad at x = 79 gives 556,907 from B and a bare table factor from A.

what_a: Returns the index of the first monster group that is currently standing, or -1 if no group is standing, ignoring the `delta` argument.
what_b: Implements R3 of the melee rules: further swings stay on the aimed group while it still has standing members, and otherwise aim shifts to the first standing group.
diff: When `aimMustMove` is false, B returns `aimedGroup` while A returns the first standing group. For example, if group 2 is aimed and standing, and group 0 is also standing, B returns 2 and A returns 0. B also depends on `aimMustMove`, which A has no counterpart for.

what_a: Returns the index of the first monster whose class matches the given class, or 0 if no monster has that class, a lookup helper with no game rule of its own.
what_b: Returns the item-descriptions index stored for a given wear class, or 0 if the class number is out of range.
diff: Not interchangeable for any input. headOfClass(ctx, cls) scans ctx.data.monsters for the first monster whose monsterClassOf() equals cls and returns its index, or 0 if none match. maxWornOfClass(ctx, c) returns ctx.data.itemDescriptions[c].index, or 0 if c is negative or past the end of itemDescriptions. Both return 0 on failure, but they read different tables and compute different values.

what_a: Converts an integer to its decimal string form, with no game meaning.
what_b: Converts a signed 64-bit integer to its decimal string representation, prefixing a minus sign for negatives, with no game meaning.
diff: For every i32 value, both return the same decimal string (including "0" and "-2147483648"), so A can replace B at A's call sites. Replacing B with A changes results for i64 values outside the i32 range, because A's parameter silently truncates them (e.g., 4294967296 becomes "0"). Separately, B has undefined behaviour for INT64_MIN because -v overflows, and A has no such case.

what_a: Maps a wearer's alignment (Good, Neutral, or Evil) to the alignment bit that item alignment restrictions are checked against, per game rule R11.
what_b: Decides whether an item counts toward a character's resistance by checking if the item's alignment flags include the wearer's own alignment bit.
diff: Function A returns a `u32` alignment bit for a given `Align`, while Function B returns a `bool` saying whether `item.alignFlags` intersects that bit. Their return types and purposes differ, so no call site can swap one for the other. Function B is built on Function A and is not a variant of it.

what_a: Converts a 1-based item alignment value (Good, Neutral, Evil) into a 0-based pen index by subtracting one.
what_b: Checks whether a guild accepts a character's alignment by testing the guild's alignment bitmask for the bit matching that alignment (Good, Neutral, or Evil), per SRD rule R15.
diff: The return types differ: A returns an i32 pen index (Good→0, Neutral→1, Evil→2), while B returns a bool membership test. They take different argument types (ItemAlign vs. Align plus a GuildDef) and their indexing bases differ (1-based vs. 0-based), so no input gives matching results at a call site.

what_a: Reports whether a monster group in the current encounter is still standing, meaning it has at least one living member, and returns false for any out-of-range group index.
what_b: If the actor's aimed monster group has no standing monsters left, retargets the actor to the first group that still has standing monsters (rule R15).
diff: groupStanding is a pure predicate that returns bool and never modifies state, while retarget returns void and writes `actor.order.aimedGroup`. Inputs where they cannot substitute: `groupStanding(game, g)` returns true for any in-range group with livingCount > 0, but `retarget` does nothing in that case, so it never changes the aim. For an actor aimed at an out-of-range group (for example -1 or kMaxGroups), `groupStanding` returns false, but `retarget` reassigns the aim to the first standing group when one exists. Also, `retarget` depends on `standingGroupIndex`, which `groupStanding` does not.

what_a: Compares two strings for equality ignoring trailing spaces and letter case, a generic text helper that the roster name matching uses.
what_b: Compares two strings for exact equality by checking that their lengths match and that one starts with the other.
diff: A ignores trailing spaces and ASCII case, so sameName("Bob", "bob") and sameName("Bob ", "Bob") return true, while seerSameText returns false for both (if seerStartsWith is a plain case-sensitive prefix test, B is exact equality). Both return true for identical strings, and both return false when lengths differ after A's trailing-space trim. A trims only ' ', not tabs. Behaviour of seerStartsWith was not provided and is assumed here.

what_a: Converts an integer to its decimal string form, with no game meaning.
what_b: Converts a 64-bit signed integer to its plain decimal string form, with a leading minus for negatives, without relying on the standard library's number formatting.
diff: For every i32 input (including 0, negatives, and INT_MIN = -2147483648) both return identical decimal text. They differ only in domain: B accepts i64 values outside the i32 range (e.g. 3000000000 gives "3000000000" from B, but A cannot take that value without narrowing and changing it), so B can replace A everywhere, but A cannot replace B at call sites that pass such values.

what_a: Dispatches the typed "pen" command, routing "pen buy" and "pen sell" to their handlers and returning a usage message to the player when the subcommand is missing or unrecognized.
what_b: Parses the typed "give" command, dispatching "give gold" and "give item" to their handlers and replying with usage text when the subcommand is missing or unrecognized.
diff: Both functions return the same way only in the sense that each delegates to its own subcommand handler. For inputs with fewer than 2 words, A returns false with a pen usage message, while B returns true with kGiveUsage. For an unknown subcommand, A returns false with the pen usage message, while B returns true with kGiveUsage. A routes "buy"/"sell" to cmdPenBuy/cmdPenSell, while B routes "gold"/"item" to giveGold/giveItem, so for any input that is not a bare or unknown subcommand, the results differ entirely.

what_a: Finds the index of the last monster in the monster table whose floor is at or above the given tier's threshold, marking where the monster list for that tier ends (SRD R51), returning -1 if the first monster is already deeper than the tier.
what_b: Converts a tier value into an item band using the formula Int(tier / 1.5) + 1, per rule R47 of the Mordor SRD.
diff: They return different kinds of values for essentially all inputs. endOfTier returns a monster-array index (or -1, or count-1), while itemBand returns a band number, Int(tier/1.5)+1. Example: with monster floors [1, 2, 4] and tier 3, endOfTier returns 1 (the index before the first monster deeper than 3), but itemBand(3) returns 3.

what_a: Returns true when the given x and y coordinates fall within the map bounds (1 to kMapWidth horizontally, 1 to height vertically).
what_b: Returns whether the given x,y coordinates fall inside the bounds of the floor state's map grid, a simple container bounds check with no game meaning.
diff: none in behaviour. B takes a `FloorState` and derives the height via `stateHeight(floor)`, while A takes the height directly, so B(floor, x, y) equals A(x, y, stateHeight(floor)) for all inputs. The only difference is the argument form.

what_a: Returns the race definition for the given character race by indexing into the loaded race table, which supplies that race's stat minimums, maximums, and bonus points used in character creation.
what_b: Checks whether a given race may take a given alignment by looking up that race's alignment mask, which is the game's rule R5 for character creation.
diff: Return types differ (`const RaceDef&` vs `bool`), so no call site can swap one for the other. A returns a reference to a race definition from `ctx.data.races`, while B returns whether an alignment is permitted from the static `kAlignMask` table. B also takes an `Align` argument that A lacks, and B ignores `ctx`.

what_a: Parses a typed string as a whole number and reports whether it is a valid 1-based pack slot (1 to 39), storing it in the slot index.
what_b: Converts a 0-based pack index into a 1-based player slot number by adding one, with no game meaning of its own.
diff: Given the same number k, A("k") returns k for k in 1..39, while B(k) returns k+1 (e.g. A("5") gives 5 and B(5) gives 6). A also rejects inputs outside 1..39 and unparseable strings by returning false, while B validates nothing and accepts any i32.

what_a: Builds the INI-style lookup key "option." followed by the given option name, with no game meaning of its own.
what_b: Returns the stored text value for a game-option INI key at index i, falling back to "(default)" for the volume index and "0" otherwise.
diff: Every input differs. A returns the string "option." + name, while B returns the stored text for index i from storedOr, or "(default)" when i == kFxVolumeIndex and "0" otherwise.

what_a: Returns true while any encounter group still has living monsters, so the combat round continues, and returns false once every group is cleared, which ends the round.
what_b: Returns the index of the first living monster in group `gi` of an encounter (the one with hits above zero), or -1 if the group index is invalid or no member is still alive.
diff: Different return types (bool vs. i32 index) and inputs: A takes no group index and checks all kMaxGroups groups via livingCount, while B takes a group index gi, returns -1 for out-of-range gi, and scans that group's monsters for the first with hits > 0. A returns true whenever any group has livingCount > 0; B can never return a bool-equivalent answer across groups.

what_a: Reports whether a monster group still has at least one living member, which the game's melee rules (R2, R3, R5) use to decide if the group keeps fighting.
what_b: Returns the index of the first living monster in group `gi` of an encounter (the one with hits above zero), or -1 if the group index is invalid or no member is still alive.
diff: Return types differ: A returns `bool` and B returns `i32` (an index or -1), so A's `true` cannot be passed where B's index is used, and vice versa. Even as "is anyone alive" predicates they can disagree: A reads the cached `g.livingCount` field, while B scans `enc.monsters[].hits`, so they diverge if the counter is stale. B also returns -1 for an out-of-range `gi` or a group that is empty or clipped by `enc.monsters.size()`, which A has no equivalent for, since it takes a group reference rather than an index.

what_a: Looks up a party member slot by a 1-based number or a case-insensitive character name, returning its 0-based index or -1 if no member matches.
what_b: Converts a 1-based player slot number to a 0-based pack index by subtracting one, with no game rule applied beyond the slot numbering convention.
diff: For a numeric token, the two agree only when the number is in range: A("3") and B(3) both give 2 for a 4-member party. They diverge for any number outside 1..p.size: A("5") with size 4 returns -1, but B(5) returns 4 (and A(0) and B(0) both return -1 only by coincidence). A also accepts character names (A("Bob") returns the matching index, or -1 if none), which B cannot take at all. B has no party argument and no bounds check.

what_a: Reinterprets a signed 32-bit integer as an unsigned 32-bit integer for indexing, with no game meaning.
what_b: Converts a 32-bit signed integer to its decimal string form, with a leading minus sign for negatives and "0" for zero.
diff: Every input differs in kind. uidx returns a u32 (for negative i the result is 2^32 + i, e.g. uidx(-1) = 4294967295), while gearNum returns a decimal string (gearNum(-1) = "-1", gearNum(42) = "42"). Neither can stand in for the other at any call site without rewriting it.

what_a: Builds the featureState lookup key string "hall.<k>.<field>" from a record index and field name, with no game rule applied.
what_b: Looks up a string value stored under a constructed "hall.<k>.<field>" key in the session's feature state, returning an empty string if the key is absent.
diff: Not interchangeable for any input. A returns the key string "hall.<k>.<field>" without touching the session, while B looks that key up in s.featureState and returns the stored value, or an empty Str if the key is absent.

what_a: Computes a character's effective resistance percentage against one damage kind by starting from the race's base value, replacing it with a fixed 90 if a counting item applies, and then taking the higher of that and the character's spell-raised resistance.
what_b: Tests whether an item's resistance bitmask grants resistance to a given damage kind, returning false for out-of-range kinds.
diff: Not comparable at any call site. Function A returns an i32 resistance percentage built from race base, gear replacement, and spell raise. Function B returns a bool, true if the item resistance bitmask has the bit for the damage kind. Their return types and purposes differ.

what_a: Checks whether a guild member's experience has reached the threshold required for the next level, returning true if so (R20.3).
what_b: Checks whether a character's guild membership can advance to the next level, returning false at the guild's maximum level and otherwise true only when the membership's experience meets the threshold from the level-up formula for its current level, race, and guild.
diff: Function A returns true whenever membership.experience >= xpRequired, with no level cap and no fixed threshold. Function B returns false when m.level >= kGuildMaxLevel, and otherwise compares experience against fn12A1(level, guild, race), which is computed from the member's level, guild, and race and ignores the caller's xpRequired. So they differ at least when the member is at max level (A may return true, B returns false), and whenever xpRequired differs from fn12A1(level, g, race) (for example, a member with experience 500 and xpRequired 400 gets true from A, but B may return false if the level's threshold is above 500). Also, A takes a GuildMembership and a raw threshold, while B takes a Character and Guild and derives the threshold itself, so the argument forms are not interchangeable.

what_a: Handles the player's bank command in town, letting them deposit gold from their on-hand purse to the bank or withdraw gold from the bank to on hand, with validation messages for refusals and overflow.
what_b: Charges gold from the character's purse, taking from gold on hand first and then from the bank, and refuses the charge without taking anything if the purse can't cover the amount.
diff: They serve different purposes. doBank moves gold between hand and bank (deposit: hand to bank; withdraw: bank to hand) and never changes the total purse. chargePurse removes an amount from the total purse, taking from hand first and then bank, and never moves gold into the bank. Examples: with hand=0 and bank=100, withdrawing 10 gives hand=10, bank=90 from doBank, but chargePurse(10) gives hand=0, bank=90. With hand=50 and bank=100, deposit 10 gives hand=40, bank=110, while chargePurse(10) gives hand=40, bank=100. doBank rejects non-positive amounts, while chargePurse(0) returns true with no change. doBank reports results via reply, while chargePurse returns bool.

what_a: Searches a list of floor states for the one whose dungeon level matches the given level and returns its index, or -1 if none matches.
what_b: Scans the game's item table in order and returns the index of the first item whose type matches and whose floor is at least a given minimum, or -1 if none qualifies.
diff: Function A matches an exact `dungeonLevel == level` on a `Vec<FloorState>`, while Function B matches `type == type` and `floor >= low` on `d.items` via accessors. B uses a threshold where A uses equality, and they read different containers and fields. For example, A with level 3 can match only floor 3, while B with low 3 matches any item on floor 3 or deeper.

what_a: At a new guild level, rolls whether the player gets a quest (or is let off), then assigns a defeat-a-monster or fetch-an-item target from the quest tier.
what_b: Assigns a guild quest to the player's membership by resetting the quest to an empty kind and recording only the guild level, since the quest kinds, targets and counts are not defined in the source text.
diff: They differ on every input. Function A never sets `quest.level` to `guildLevel` (it sets `tier = questTier(guildLevel)`, and only on the success paths), while B always sets `quest.level = guildLevel`. On a successful Defeat or Fetch roll, A also sets `kind`, `target`, and `state = Active` and B does not. A also emits `guilds.quest_let_off` or `guilds.quest_fetch` messages, which B never does. Even when A's roll yields no quest, A leaves `level` at its cleared value while B records `guildLevel`.

what_a: If the actor's aimed monster group has no standing monsters left, retargets the actor to the first group that still has standing monsters (rule R15).
what_b: Returns the index of the first monster group that is currently standing, or -1 if no group is standing, ignoring the `delta` argument.
diff: Function A (`retarget`) returns void and may modify `actor.order.aimedGroup`, while Function B (`standingGroupIndex`) returns an index (or -1) and has no side effects. Their return types and purposes differ, so no input makes them interchangeable.

what_a: Reports whether a monster group in the current encounter is still standing, meaning it has at least one living member, and returns false for any out-of-range group index.
what_b: Builds the text summary of the current monster encounter for the player, listing each monster group with its name, count, state, living count, and which party member is aimed at it.
diff: Function A is a bool predicate that returns true only for a valid group index with livingCount > 0. Function B builds a multi-line Str report of monster groups and the party members aimed at them, so no input makes them return the same kind of result.

what_a: Clears the pending seer person offer (its kind, name, and level) from the session's feature state once the offer has been answered.
what_b: Registers the town-screen "seer" command, which lets the player search for a creature, item, or person for a fee, and answer yes or no to a pending offer.
diff: Function A erases three session state keys (kSeerKindKey, kSeerNameKey, kSeerLevelKey) and returns nothing. Function B registers the "seer" command with the feature system. No input makes them produce the same result.

what_a: Copies named integer and string fields and one integer array from a parsed JSON object into a SpellDef record, a generated loader that maps spell-table data fields onto struct members.
what_b: Copies the `spawnMask` and `lairId` integer fields from a parsed JSON object into a FloorArea struct, with no game rule applied beyond reading the values.
diff: They read different types and fill different fields. A populates tableIndex, name, id, category, level, u4, killEffect, affectMonster, affectGroup, damage1, damage2, specialEffect, effect, required (array), and resistIndex on a SpellDef. B populates only spawnMask and lairId on a FloorArea. No input produces matching results.

what_a: At a new guild level, rolls whether the player gets a quest (or is let off), then assigns a defeat-a-monster or fetch-an-item target from the quest tier.
what_b: Checks whether a character's current guild quest (none, defeat a monster, or fetch an item) is satisfied, and when asked to consume, removes the fetched item from the pack and increments the character's item-quest count.
diff: Function A (assignQuest) clears and assigns a new quest, while Function B (questSatisfied) checks whether the current quest is complete and may consume a fetch item. They never produce comparable results: for example, B returns a bool and never writes quest state, while A returns void and writes kind, target, level, and state. Their only overlap is that both read `membership.quest.kind`.

what_a: Lets a payer buy back one penned companion of a monster type, charging a price based on the creature's base worth and how many are already penned, then freeing one pen slot.
what_b: Confinement sell pens one companion into the pen for its alignment, checks the pen cap, prices the sale from the creature's base worth and the number already penned, and pays the gold to the town income payee.
diff: Function A takes a companion out of a pen and charges the payer, while Function B puts a companion into a pen and pays a payee, so they have opposite effects on pens and gold for every input. A also prices with `penBuyPrice` on the pen count and releases a slot, whereas B prices with `penSellPrice` on the pre-sale count and the companion's `idLevel`, and penns a slot. A validates `monsterRef` directly, while B validates `companion.ref` and `companion.monsterId` separately.

what_a: Looks up a string value by key in the session's feature-state map and returns it, or a supplied default if the key is absent.
what_b: Reads a numeric field from a JSON object by key, returning its value as a double or 0.0 if the key is absent.
diff: Not applicable. A looks up a string key in a session's featureState map and returns the stored Str or the caller's default Str. B looks up a key in a JSON object and returns asDouble() of that value, or 0.0 if the key is absent. The return types differ (Str vs double), the inputs differ (Session map vs JsonValue), and the fallbacks differ (caller-supplied string vs fixed 0.0).

what_a: Returns whether the given x,y coordinates fall inside the bounds of the floor state's map grid, a simple container bounds check with no game meaning.
what_b: Checks whether a given square on a dungeon floor (1-based x, y coordinates) has a specific flag set, returning false for out-of-bounds coordinates.
diff: A returns whether (x, y) lies inside the state's map bounds, so it is true for every in-bounds cell regardless of content. B returns whether the cell at (x, y) has a given flag bit set, so it is false for in-bounds cells that lack that flag, and it also applies the 1-based index math. For example, (1, 1) on a 10-wide floor gives true from A, but B gives true only if that cell's flags include `flag`.

what_a: Returns the index of the first entry in a list of names that matches a given word, ignoring case, or -1 if none match.
what_b: Scans the game data's item list for the entry whose id matches the given id and returns a pointer to it, or null if none matches.
diff: Function A returns the index of the first name in `names` that matches `word` (via `sameName`), or -1. Function B returns a pointer to the first `data.items` entry whose `id` equals the given `id`, or nullptr. They match on different keys (a string name versus an integer id), search different collections, and return different types, so no input gives the same result for both.

what_a: Searches a list of floor states for the one whose dungeon level matches the given level and returns its index, or -1 if none matches.
what_b: Returns the index of the first item in the item definition table whose type matches the given kind, or -1 if none does.
diff: Inputs differ in kind: A takes `(Vec<FloorState>, i32 level)` and matches `floors[i].dungeonLevel == level`; B takes `(Ctx, i32 kind)` and matches `static_cast<i32>(ctx.data.items[i].type) == kind`. So A can never be called with a `Ctx` or B with a floor vector, and any input that is valid for one is invalid for the other.

what_a: Returns the rarity value of the item at the given index in the game data, which the chest-item generation logic uses as a weight when choosing loot.
what_b: Picks a random item for a treasure chest by rolling an item type, finding the matching records within the chest's value band, and choosing one weighted by rarity, restarting the whole generation if nothing fits.
diff: Function A returns a `double`, the rarity of one item record at index `idx`, and has no other effects. Function B returns an `Item` (a chest drop) and consumes RNG draws. Their return types differ, so no call site of one can take the other without a rewrite. B calls A internally to weight its random pick.

what_a: Joins the words of a typed command from index `from` onward into a single string separated by spaces, which lets a multi-word guild name be passed as one argument.
what_b: Joins the words of a string vector from a given starting index into one space-separated string.
diff: none

what_a: Checks whether the typed text is a case-insensitive prefix of a person's name, which the seer uses to match a player's answer against the pending person offer.
what_b: Parses the player's typed "seer" command, showing usage help, answering the Seer's pending offer with yes or no, or dispatching a paid search for a creature, item, or person.
diff: Not interchangeable for any input. seerStartsWith is a pure, case-insensitive prefix test on two strings, while seerCommand is a command dispatcher that takes a Session and writes a reply string, and it can call seerAnswer, seerSearchThing, or seerSearchPerson.

what_a: Checks whether a party member number entered for a typed swap falls within the valid 1-to-kPartyMaxSize range of party slots.
what_b: Parses a 1-based party member number typed as a string, checks it falls within the party size, and converts it to a 0-based index.
diff: (1) Bounds: A accepts any member in 1..kPartyMaxSize, while B accepts only 1..s.game.party.size. With a party of 3 and kPartyMaxSize of 6, member 4 gives true in A and false in B. (2) Input: A takes an already-parsed i32 and returns only a validity bool, while B parses a string, rejects non-numeric input, and writes the 0-based index to idx. (3) A's 1-based assumption is unverified, though B confirms 1-based numbering.

what_a: Handles a typed "claim <member>" command by checking the named character's Nomad guild membership and attempting to give them the Nomad guildmastership, then replying with a message to the player.
what_b: Forfeit removes a character's membership in a guild (unless it is not joined or is the base Nomad guild), resets that membership to defaults including guild gold, and drops the active guild back to Nomad if it was the one forfeited.
diff: They do different things. cmdClaim is a command handler that takes a guildmastership for a named member, returns true and sets a reply string, and never resets membership. Forfeit takes a Character and Guild, resets that guild's membership to defaults, may fall back activeGuild to Nomad, and returns true or false depending on whether the guild was joined and is not Nomad.

what_a: Resolves a player's typed guild argument, either a numeric index or a guild name compared case-insensitively, to a valid guild index for the guild log command, returning false if no valid guild matches.
what_b: Returns the guild membership record for the given character and guild, looked up by indexing the character's guild array with the guild's numeric value.
diff: Function A parses a string argument (a numeric index or a case-insensitive guild name) into an index, returning false on empty, out-of-range, or unknown input. Function B takes an already-typed `Guild` value and returns a reference to `ch.guilds[g]` with no bounds check. They do not share inputs, outputs, or purpose, so no argument-form change would make one a substitute for the other.

what_a: Checks whether the typed text names a valid pack slot (2 through kPackSlots, since slot 1 is the Hands) for a give command and returns that slot number, or -1 to signal "No Item to give!".
what_b: Refuses a pack slot of 1 (the hands, not an item) by setting the player-facing reply "Slot 1 is your hands, not an item." and returning false, otherwise accepting the slot.
diff: giveSlot parses text and returns a slot number in 2..kPackSlots or -1, while gearSlotOk takes an integer and returns only whether it is not slot 1. Inputs where they differ: slot 0 gives -1 from giveSlot but true from gearSlotOk; slot 1 gives -1 from giveSlot but false from gearSlotOk (with the hands message); slot kPackSlots+1 or higher gives -1 from giveSlot but true from gearSlotOk; slots 2..kPackSlots give a valid number from giveSlot and true from gearSlotOk; non-numeric text can only be rejected by giveSlot.

what_a: Plans gifts of gold from other party members to cover a payer's shortfall in a town charge, and if the plan is complete, moves the gold and logs one message per giver.
what_b: Plans how a party member's shortfall in gold for a town charge is covered by other city-based party members' bank gold (R35), returning the gift plan without moving any money, and only when mod hooks are live and the party has at least two members.
diff: The return value is identical for every input, since A returns the plan that B computes. They differ in side effects: whenever B reports covered with at least one gift, A also subtracts each gift from the giver's goldInBank, adds it to the payer's goldOnHand, and emits one ctx.say line per gift. B changes nothing and emits nothing.

what_a: Ticks the ailment timer for the player's game state, skipping the tick if one is already running, and emits an "Ailment tick" event using the ailment interval, with the actual ailment effects left to a separate module.
what_b: Advances the game's combat, play, and ailment clocks by the elapsed milliseconds, running combat rounds while a fight is on, ticking the play clock when it crosses a 250 ms boundary, and applying ailment ticks.
diff: Their purposes differ. `ailmentTick` handles one ailment tick: it sets a re-entrancy guard, emits a `clock.ailment_tick` event, and clears the guard. `advanceTime` advances the combat clock (running `combatTick` and `settleRound` per boundary when in combat), the play clock, and then calls `ailmentTick` once per accumulated ailment interval. Their signatures also differ: `(Ctx&, GameState&)` versus `(Session&, i64 ms)`. A cannot replace B at any call site, and B does far more than A.

what_a: Packs an item's seven boolean flags into a single integer bitmask (guildIssued=1, aligned=2, chestTeleporter=4, destructible=8, equipped=16, lost=32, slotCursed=64) for saving.
what_b: Unpacks a 7-bit flag integer into the seven boolean item states (guild-issued, aligned, chest teleporter, destructible, equipped, lost, slot-cursed) on an item.
diff: Function A maps an Item to a bitmask and Function B maps a bitmask back onto an Item; they are inverse operations, not equivalent. Calling A where B is expected (or vice versa) returns a value or mutates an Item in ways that do not match, e.g. A(item) returns an i64 while B(item, b) returns void and mutates item.

what_a: Checks whether the typed text is a case-insensitive prefix of a person's name, which the seer uses to match a player's answer against the pending person offer.
what_b: Looks up a string value by key in the session's featureState map for the seer's pending person offer, returning an empty string if the key is absent.
diff: Not interchangeable for any inputs. A is a case-insensitive prefix test returning bool; B is a map lookup returning a Str. For example, `seerStartsWith("Seer", "se")` returns true, while `seerGet(s, "se")` returns the stored value for key "se" or an empty string.

what_a: Scans a floor's squares in row-major order and reports the 1-based X/Y position of the first square whose flags include the given floor flag, returning false if none does.
what_b: Scans the game's item table in order and returns the index of the first item whose type matches and whose floor is at least a given minimum, or -1 if none qualifies.
diff: Not comparable inputs. A searches `def.fields` for a `FloorFlag` bit and returns 1-based (x, y) coordinates through out-parameters, or false. B searches `d.items` for a matching type and minimum floor and returns a record index, or -1. They operate on different data, test different predicates, and return different kinds of results.

what_a: Handles the player's typed `guildlog` command by validating its arguments, clearing the log on "clean", or otherwise printing that guild's log entries newest first with relative day prefixes, or "No Entries" if there are none.
what_b: Registers the "guildlog" town command, which shows a chosen guild's log or cleans it down to the newest 50 entries.
diff: Function A parses arguments and returns a guild log reply (or clean, or usage/error text) for any input, while Function B returns void and only registers `cmdGuildlog` as a command with the name "guildlog", the Town screen, and a help string; for every input they produce different results, since B produces no reply at all.

what_a: Converts the player's typed word "good", "neutral", or "evil" (case-insensitive) into its item alignment code, returning -1 if the word is not recognised.
what_b: Parses a typed word as either a numeric index or a case-insensitive name into a Guild enum value, returning false if neither matches a valid guild.
diff: Different purposes: A maps the words "good", "neutral", and "evil" (case-insensitive) to alignment codes and returns -1 otherwise, while B parses a number and range-checks it against kGuildCount, or else matches a guild name, returning a bool and an out-parameter. For example, "good" yields a code in A but fails in B, and "2" fails in A but may succeed in B.

what_a: Returns a reference to the inventory of the party member at the given index, converting the signed index to unsigned for container access; it has no game meaning of its own.
what_b: Returns the `floor` field of the item at the given index in the game data's item list, converting the index to an unsigned integer for lookup.
diff: Not comparable at any call site. `invAt` returns an `Inventory&` reference into `p.inventories` from a `Party`, while `itemFloor` returns an `i32` read from the `floor` field of `d.items` in a `GameData`. The two functions share only the unchecked `static_cast<u32>` index pattern.

what_a: Awards experience to a character's guild membership, capped at the guild's pin threshold, and announces when the character becomes pinned or has enough experience to make a level.
what_b: Computes the experience cap for a character's current level in a guild, which is the XP threshold for the next level minus one, scaled by the guild and race experience factors.
diff: Every input differs in kind. Function A awards experience: it mutates `m.experience`, may emit "pinned" or "enough experience to level" messages via `ctx.say`, and returns the gained amount. Function B only returns the experience cap (`levelThresholdXp(level+1) - 1`) with no side effects. A calls the same cap computation internally, but B's result is not A's result for any input.

what_a: Returns a reference to the item's definition by indexing the game's item table directly with the item's id, with no game rule applied.
what_b: Looks up an item's definition record from the game's item table by its id, returning a pointer to it or null when the id is negative or out of range.
diff: For in-range ids (0 <= id < items.size()) both return the same element. For id < 0, A converts the id to u32 and indexes out of bounds (undefined behaviour), while B returns nullptr. For id >= items.size(), A indexes out of bounds (undefined behaviour), while B returns nullptr. A returns `const ItemDef&` and B returns `const ItemDef*`, so call sites that bind or dereference the result differently will not compile without changes.

what_a: Recalculates a character's maximum spell points from their abilities, then either fully restores current spell points on refill or caps current spell points at the new maximum.
what_b: Recalculates a character's spell points, with the refill flag passed through to the casting module's overload (the actual formula is delegated and not defined in this file).
diff: none

what_a: Computes the gold cost to join a guild from the character-independent SRD R26 formula, summing weighted ability ratings and spell-class maxima, then squaring the total and scaling it by a fixed factor.
what_b: Returns the gold cost to join a given guild, looked up from a fixed per-guild table and converted to the game's internal currency scale.
diff: Inputs differ: A takes a `GuildDef` (abilities and spellMax) plus an unused `Character` and computes a formula, while B takes only a `Guild` enum and returns a hardcoded per-guild table value, so no argument-form change maps one onto the other. Results differ: A returns 0 for any definition with no abilities or spell maxima, while B returns a nonzero table value for every guild, and the two agree only if A's formula reproduces each table entry, which the sources don't establish. A's result unit is also unresolved, while B returns whole gold times `kCurrencyScale`.

what_a: Returns the fee charged to identify an item, computed from its data with a default shelf count of 1 for when no store is involved.
what_b: Computes the gold fee the Clerk charges to identify an item, set equal to the item's sell value (approximated by its market price for its alignment).
diff: Not fully determinable from the excerpts. Function A computes a store-based fee via `storeIdentifyFee` with a fixed shelf count of 1 and returns `Currency`. Function B computes `priceOfItem(ctx, item, item.alignment)` and returns `i64`, following the sell-value rule. The two results can differ for any item where `storeIdentifyFee(..., 1)` does not equal `priceOfItem(..., item.alignment)`, and the comments indicate they are not intended to match.

what_a: Checks whether a given item definition's guild mask allows a character of guild index g to use the item, by testing the corresponding bit.
what_b: Looks up in the race-guild eligibility grid (T4) whether a given race is allowed to join a given guild, returning that yes/no answer.
diff: Not comparable on the same inputs. A tests bit `g` of an item's `guilds` field (item-to-guild eligibility, taking `ItemDef` and an integer guild). B looks up a race-by-guild grid `kGuildGrid` (race-to-guild eligibility, taking `Ctx`, `Race`, and `Guild`). Their parameters, data sources, and meanings differ, so no input gives matching results across both.
